{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took ownership of the upper tail fork (stroke 3) as soon as the plan was set and built it. It is the stretch of the fish's outline that makes the tail read as a tail. I laid it from the crossing outward and re-laid it when I saw it could be cleaner, so the fork opens out gently and joins the body line without a sharp corner. I also took the diagnostic that helped the table, by pointing out that the chain stalled at the end of the start row where one domino sat too tight against the next.

Execution: I picked one piece of work and stayed on it quietly. I confirmed the plan out loud early ('I'm on the upper tail fork, stroke 3'). I traced the stroke from the pad rather than freehanding it, so the shape matched the sketch. I used several close inspections to check where the line carried on and where it ended, and I stood dominoes back up where needed. I stayed off the nose area while others worked there, so I didn't add to the bumping risk.

Collaboration: I split the tail with Hana, one fork each, and we did not overlap. I kept my messages short and useful, flagging the tight domino to Sofia with a concrete suggestion (pull it and re-seat it as she joins), then stepped back. I kept my hands off the busy start area so people working there weren't disturbed.

Leadership: I led by example on my own piece, taking a defined job, finishing it and keeping the table informed. I held back where more hands would have made things worse, and I kept the mood light so the table stayed calm in the final minutes.

I believe my share of the table's result was about a quarter. It was a meaningful part, the tail fork, and the others carried the body lines and the nose.", "my_share_percent": 25}
